key_insight: KOH {111} planes on (110) Si give litho-free, atomically smooth single-crystal walls from a wet bench. A cheap c-Si template, if a cell topology existed.
killer_doubt: At 1:160 selectivity a 3 um etch undercuts ~19 nm per side, more than a 30 nm wall. Wet drying collapses 100:1 walls. {111} Dit is ~3x (100).
decisive_experiment: E-beam lines on a (110) wafer (~$30k), TMAH/KOH etched 3 um deep with supercritical dry. Map wall thickness and taper vs depth, and Dit on {111} MOS caps. Before that, a cell topology on paper.
prior_art: Kendall (1975-79) KOH (110) vertical walls; KOH X-ray gratings; horizontal c-Si tiers via Si/SiGe epi (Samsung VS-DRAM, imec 120 bilayers) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Sense amps in logic need only ~19 mm2 of N3 for 24 GB at 8:1 muxing, and bonds at ~2 um pitch suffice per subarray. Periphery-off-array is sound.
killer_doubt: An 8:1 mux senses 1 of 8 cells a wordline destroys: serial restore pushes tRC to ~100 ns. At 95-110 C refresh rises 4-8x. Array-only dies are untestable pre-bond.
decisive_experiment: Thermal and refresh model of a 24 GB array die on a 1 kW accelerator, plus a DRAM-process subarray test chip with 8:1 mux timing sequential restore ($300k). Compare against N-40's bonded-SA wafer.
prior_art: Tezzaron DiRAM (sense amps on separate logic layer); triage N-40 MSB-DRAM and N-41 carrier-is-memory; HBM4 foundry logic base dies [training knowledge].

key_insight: CDS cancels sense-amp offset and frozen bitline kTC (0.41 mV rms on 30 fF, 85 C). A 0.5 fF cell gives 8 mV (~14 sigma): 10x less capacitor.
killer_doubt: At 0.2 fF, 64 ms allows ~250 e- loss: <=0.6 fA, ~20x below the 13 fA Si tail, so it needs an IGZO access device. WL kickback adds ~2 mV.
decisive_experiment: A 28 nm MPW (~$300k): MIM cells of 0.2/0.5/1 fF on 30 fF bitlines with a CDS versus a latch sense amp, plus dummy-WL coupling compensation. Measure BER vs Cs and temperature to 1e-9.
prior_art: Samsung and Hynix offset-cancellation sense amps in production DDR4/5; Hitachi charge-transfer pre-sensing; triage N-04, N-27 auto-zero [training knowledge].

key_insight: Open array generators and a tier/yield calculator lower the entry cost for university array research. They are useful infrastructure for this study's own models.
killer_doubt: SKY130/GF180 have no DRAM capacitor. A ~2-5 um2 MIM or gain cell is ~1,000x a 1b cell, so tape-outs teach nothing about the 13 fA tail or capacitors.
decisive_experiment: Not needed. If pursued, fund OpenGCRAM extensions plus a public parametric 3D-tier cost model (~$150k) and count external tape-outs after 12 months.
prior_art: OpenRAM (UCSC), OpenGCRAM, DRAM Bender, Ramulator, CACTI-3DD/DESTINY; similar I-05632 dropped and I-04102 held by other critics.

key_insight: Stranded DRAM and retired modules are wafer-free supply. Pooling plus redeployment matters more at ~4x contract prices.
killer_doubt: Microsoft Pond measured ~7% DRAM savings from 16-socket CXL pools, not 20-40%. DDR4 reuse behind CXL is already deployed. CXL adds ~70-150 ns latency.
decisive_experiment: None physics-relevant. A market pilot: refurbish 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs into CXL expanders and measure test fallout and $/GB vs new DDR5 (~$200k).
prior_art: Microsoft Pond (ASPLOS 2023) and GreenSKU DDR4-over-CXL reuse; Memtrade; CXL pooling appliances (UnifabriX, XConn, Samsung CMM-B) [training knowledge].

key_insight: A POM monolayer (~1e14/cm2, 2 e- each) holds ~32 uC/cm2 in a 0.3 V window, ~15x a 0.5 nm EOT dielectric. That is real only with electrolyte counter-ions.
killer_doubt: Without mobile ions, redox charge images across the dielectric: C = series(C_diel, C_redox) < C_diel, no gain. Ionic electrolytes fail endurance (1e5-1e6 cycles) and ns kinetics.
decisive_experiment: A MIM coupon, TiN/POM monolayer/ZrO2/TiN versus a no-POM control (~$50k): C-V at 1 kHz-100 MHz. Any charge above C_diel*V at 100 MHz would overturn the series argument.
prior_art: ZettaCore porphyrin memory (Bocian/Lindsey); POM flash storage nodes (Busche et al., Nature 2014); triage N-17, N-25 (pseudocapacitive variant dead) [training knowledge].

key_insight: Web lines amortise vacuum and transport at ~$1-10/m2. An IGZO 1T1C at 0.08 um2 is ~1.5 TB/m2, so area cost, not density, could set $/bit.
killer_doubt: Converter assets are <10% of a memory line. Spatial ALD and NIL run ~1-10 m/min. A 10 ppm/K web moves ~100 um/m per 10 K vs ~10 nm overlay.
decisive_experiment: Fold into I-01819's test: a two-layer self-aligned IGZO TFT array on a 30 cm web at 100 nm rules. Measure overlay, Vt sigma and particle D0 ($500k) before any converter deal.
prior_art: HP Labs SAIL roll-to-roll TFTs; PragmatIC IGZO FlexICs; Thinfilm printed memory; in-study I-01819 (advanced) and I-06468 [training knowledge].

key_insight: Decoupling tier-stack deposition from the wafer fab is a legitimate capital idea. Web coaters deposit area at ~100x lower cost.
killer_doubt: Packaging coatings carry >=1 pinhole/cm2; 128 tiers need <0.01/cm2/layer or every die shorts. A 1 um particle voids ~mm2 on lamination. The stack is ~5% of wafer cost.
decisive_experiment: Web-coat a 16-pair Mo/SiOx stack on polyimide, transfer it to a Si wafer, and measure pinhole shorts/cm2, bond-void density and thickness sigma per layer ($150k). Kill if shorts exceed 0.1/cm2/layer.
prior_art: Roll-to-roll vacuum metallizing and barrier films; 3D NAND PECVD ON stacks; in-study I-10786 and I-07806 dropped laminated/wound stacks [training knowledge].

key_insight: Strain-driven self-rolling compacts a planar array 10-30x in footprint with one release etch. That could matter where footprint under an accelerator is scarce.
killer_doubt: Rolling creates no bits: 20 turns need 20x the patterned area, so $/bit equals planar thin-film cost. R=5 um bends a 100 nm stack ~1%. Inner-turn contacts are unsolved.
decisive_experiment: Roll a 1 mm2 IGZO TFT test array (5 turns) and measure Vt shift vs radius and edge-contact yield per turn ($100k). Note that a pass still leaves cost per bit unchanged.
prior_art: Rolled-up nanomembranes (Prinz; Schmidt, IFW Dresden): rolled capacitors and microbatteries; duplicate of I-00027 (dropped elsewhere) [training knowledge].

key_insight: RT Coulomb blockade needs E_c >~10 kT, which a ~2 nm Si island achieves. SETs are superb charge meters only for charge placed directly on their island or gate.
killer_doubt: At the bitline foot the SET reads bitline voltage. A ~0.03 aF gate means a ~5 V period: a 33 mV signal moves ~0.006 e. Offset charge varies per device.
decisive_experiment: Paper first: input-referred voltage noise of an RT SET versus a minimum MOSFET on a 3 fF node, including offset-charge drift. If you persist, put the SET inside the cell as gain (PADOX test chip, $200k).
prior_art: NTT PADOX SETs (Takahashi 1995); Hitachi single-electron memory 128 Mb prototype (Yano, ISSCC 1998); RT Si SETs (~2 nm islands) [training knowledge].

key_insight: LLM decode reads every weight and KV byte once per token in fixed order, so a ~33 ms loop fits. Per-lap regeneration doubles as refresh. Shifts cost ~86 fJ/bit.
killer_doubt: It needs serial arrays that exist: imec IGZO CCDs show CTE ~98%, and a 64-stage lap needs >=0.999. Unpredictable 20-40% of traffic sees ~10 us without a front tier.
decisive_experiment: Trace-driven simulator ($150k) of decode, prefill and training traces on a serial-string array (shift rate, CTE, lap length) with an SRAM front buffer. Report the bytes served within 30 ns-equivalent and pJ/bit vs HBM.
prior_art: IBM 650 SOAP; 1970s CCD/bubble major-minor loops; ShiftsReduce racetrack placement (Khan et al., TACO 2019) (via search snippet); none found for LLM-sweep timing.

key_insight: A capacitorless heterostructure bit per tier at ~17 nm2/bit would be the ideal 3D cell. The crystalline band offset avoids oxide charge-fluence wear.
killer_doubt: Strained Ge gives dEv ~0.74 eV: tau ~ 1e-13 s * exp(0.74/0.031) ~ 2 ms at 85 C. 1 s needs >=0.92 eV. Ge ni (~2000x Si) refills empty wells.
decisive_experiment: Measure hole retention vs temperature in a Si/Si0.3Ge0.7 QW capacitorless test FET (university epi, $150k). Extract the activation energy; kill unless Ea >=0.9 eV. A wide-gap (GaN/AlN) host is the workaround.
prior_art: Ertosun and Saraswat 1T-QW DRAM with SiGe hole well (Stanford, EDL 2008); floating-body ZRAM; Si/SiGe superlattice 3D DRAM stacks [training knowledge].
